title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025
short_title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill changes the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to remove customs duties on goods brought in under the Geelong Treaty, a nuclear submarine partnership agreement with the United Kingdom signed on 26 July 2025.

It adds a new concessional item to Schedule 4 of the Act, setting a 'Free' duty rate for goods used under the treaty, which helps Australia meet its treaty obligations to avoid certain taxes and charges.

The duty waiver starts on the later of the day after the bill receives Royal Assent or the day the treaty enters into force, and applies only to goods not yet cleared through customs with duties calculated at that time.
changes: Amends the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to implement a customs duty waiver for goods imported under the Geelong Treaty.
Inserts a new concessional item 58A into Schedule 4, prescribing a free rate of duty for goods used under the treaty.
Sets the waiver to take effect on the later of the day after Royal Assent or the treaty's entry into force.
summary.affected: Importers of goods used under the Geelong Treaty, which involves the Australian and United Kingdom governments.

speeches.speaker: Julian Hill
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025, which would amend the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to provide a free rate of duty for goods used under the Geelong treaty and implement Australia's customs obligations under the agreement.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025 and Freedom of Information Amendment Bill 2025 would stand referred to the Federation Chamber after debate on each second-reading motion was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders so the Freedom of Information Amendment Bill 2025 could be debated in the House, arguing that referring it to the Federation Chamber would reduce scrutiny of proposed restrictions on access to government information and undermine transparency.

speeches.speaker: Pat Conaghan
speeches.brief: Supported passage of the Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025, arguing that it would implement article XXI of the Geelong treaty by providing duty-free treatment for qualifying goods and support Australia's AUKUS cooperation with the United Kingdom and the United States.

speeches.speaker: Matt Burnell
speeches.brief: Supported the Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025, arguing it gives domestic effect to the Geelong treaty, enables tariff-free movement of AUKUS materials, supports submarine construction and associated jobs, and strengthens Australia's industrial, skills and security capacity. The bill was agreed to and ordered to be reported without amendment.

speeches.speaker: Karen Grogan
speeches.brief: Presented the Selection of Bills Committee's eighth report, recommending referral of the Copyright Amendment Bill 2025 for inquiry by 19 December 2025, and recorded competing proposals concerning referrals of the Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025 and the Fair Work Amendment (Right to Work from Home) Bill 2025.

speeches.speaker: Katy Gallagher
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend specified standing-order provisions so the Customs Tariff Amendment (Geelong Treaty Implementation) Bill 2025 could be considered during the sittings.

speeches.speaker: Tim Ayres
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of bills implementing customs duty arrangements under the Geelong Treaty and establishing a Parliamentary Joint Committee on Defence with classified-information safeguards and oversight functions; debate was adjourned.
